subject: Neurolytics DPA: sandboxed telemetry carveout + no-model-learning scope
messages:
From: Alex Tran <alex.tran@neurolytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@neurolytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA redline and carveout questions

Sean — thanks for sending the DPA. Attached is a redline from our side (Neurolytics_DPA_redline_v3.docx). A few points we need to confirm before legal can sign: 

1) No-model-learning carveout: we need a firm commitment that our prompts/responses will not be used to improve or retrain reachable model weights, unless expressly authorized. Can Redwood confirm language that covers downstream internal retraining (including feature-store tracing, analytics aggregates)?

2) Telemetry and usage logs: we understand you collect anonymized telemetry for platform health. We need the ability to opt out of telemetry capture for our tenant and, when telemetry is retained for troubleshooting, to have it stored in a sandboxed tenant view (separate from global training buckets).

3) Subprocessors: please provide the current subprocessor CSV and confirm onshore routing for KMS keys if we choose "onshore KMS" in the DPA.

We attached a CSV template of the inventory we expect to map to your list. Also copying procurement for timing — our target is to close legal signoff and PO by 08/20.

Thanks,
Alex Tran
Head of Security & Privacy
Neurolytics

Attachments: Neurolytics_DPA_redline_v3.docx, subprocessor_inventory_neurolytics.csv

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tran <alex.tran@neurolytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline and carveout questions

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then next steps: 

- No-model-learning carveout: we can accept a strict "no-model-learning" clause scoped to tenant inputs and outputs (prompts, responses, session traces) as long as we retain minimal operational telemetry for platform reliability. We propose a carveout that prevents any use of tenant data for model updates across our model catalog (hosted and dedicated) unless Neurolytics gives explicit written consent. 

- Sandboxed telemetry: we can enable a tenant-level telemetry sandbox. That would route diagnostic logs and any stored traces to a segregated bucket with restricted roles. We need to confirm retention windows and whether your SRE/Support can access ephemeral troubleshooting sessions. 

- Subprocessors & KMS: attaching current subprocessor inventory and a proposal for onshore KMS routing options. Dev, can you confirm estimated lead time for KMS onshore key provisioning and any cost delta?

Proposed next steps: 
- Kimberly to provide redline language for the no-train clause (legal).
- Marissa to agree on timeline & commercial impact for reserved capacity / onshore KMS.
- Dev to confirm ops feasibility (sandboxed logs, retention).

We aim to give you a revised DPA with specific redline language by EOD 08/11. If procurement needs a mutual action plan we can share one.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_redwood_current.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T13:15:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline and carveout questions

Team — drafting guidance below for the redline language and a few legal caveats. This is a working draft for internal review, not client-facing yet.

Draft clause (plain language summary): 
- "No-model-learning": Redwood will not use Neurolytics' tenant-generated prompts, responses, or conversation transcripts to update, fine-tune, or otherwise improve the parameters or weights of any model used to serve other customers or our public model catalog. Redwood may collect anonymized, aggregated telemetry for platform monitoring that cannot be reverse-engineered to derive tenant inputs.

Caveats / follow-ups: 
- We should define "anonymized" and give examples of telemetry fields (CPU/GPU metrics, kernel failures, per-request latency, token counts) that are excluded from the carveout. 
- If Neurolytics requests onshore KMS, we must map out a provisioning SLA (we typically need 3-4 weeks for key setup in a new tenant). Any onshore KMS implies a modest monthly premium for dedicated key management.
- Subprocessor inventory: ensure we confirm whether any of our infra vendors perform model improvement tasks (some third parties run experiments; we'll list them and mark "no access to tenant inputs").

I will prepare a legal redline for the attached Neurolytics document and aim to circulate to Alex by tomorrow EOD.

-Kimberly
Associate General Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tran <alex.tran@neurolytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@neurolytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline and carveout questions

Alex — looping commercial and ops. Appreciate the target close date; to make that feasible here's a short mutual action plan we can both agree to: 

1) 08/11 — Redwood legal sends formal redline implementing the no-model-learning clause and definitions. (Owner: Kimberly)
2) 08/12 — Ops sync: Dev to confirm sandboxed telemetry architecture and retention window (owner: Dev Patel).
3) 08/13 — Commercial update: Marissa to provide a summary of any pricing delta for onshore KMS + reserved capacity (owner: Marissa).
4) 08/14 — Final DPA and PO path: Neurolytics to confirm internal signers; Redwood to prepare DocuSign.

Notes: 
- If Neurolytics needs an explicit export-control / cross-border routing section, we can add a short addendum specifying that Neurolytics data is processed in US regions unless they request EU residency (separate statement).
- For procurement: we can provision a limited trial with telemetry sandboxing enabled immediately for a 2-week POC while legal completes redlines — this helps unblock integration testing.

Let us know if we should push any dates earlier. Happy to jump on a 20-min call today to align.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mutual_action_plan_NEU-4521.xlsx

From: Alex Tran <alex.tran@neurolytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@neurolytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline and carveout questions

Marissa / team — thanks, that MAP looks good and is actionable for us. A few clarifications before we move the PO: 

- Trial POC: yes to the 2-week sandboxed telemetry POC. We will provide test data and a short checklist for validation.
- Redline: Kimberly, please include explicit language that prohibits both (a) training downstream public models and (b) training internal experimental models unless Neurolytics provides prior written consent. We need explicit mention of derived analytics vs model updates — derived analytics for usage patterns is acceptable if pseudonymized and aggregated.
- KMS: we will request onshore KMS. Please confirm the monthly fee and any lead time; procurement needs the cost to finalize the PO.

If you can send DocuSign by 08/14 (as proposed) we can route signatures the same week. Attaching our procurement contact for next steps.

Regards,
Alex Tran
Head of Security & Privacy
Neurolytics

Attachment references: PO-ready PDF will be requested after redline acceptance
